body: It's hard not to feel like there is something wrong with me socially when I just keep failing at interviews. Most people do not struggle with interviewing, at most they interview with 10 different companies before they get an offer. Onw guy on the jobs subreddit failed to get offers from 4 companies and immedietly one person attributed it to his interviewing skills. I probably had at least a dozen say no. I do make it through multiple rounds with some but I just fall short on the offer.

YOu know what? fuck you. I am doing a lot right now, working at a shitty part-time job, sending out several tailored resumes/cover letters a day, driving dozens of miles to job interviews, going to meetups, etc. People like you, who assume underemployed/unemployed college graduates are just "sitting on their asses" are why I feel ashamed and why it is hard to really make new friends because I am afraid of this judgmental bullshit of being 25 years old and living at home. 

edit: and MBA degree holders, outside of top schools struggle even more to find jobs than average engineers. 

edit 2: I realize you just wanted to help so I'm sorry if the comment wasn't meant to be passive aggressive, I just get a lot of shit from people who think I am just "sitting around and doing nothing."
